resale_co.name: Resale MCCO Certificate (Municipal Certificate of Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Shrewsbury Township Code Enforcement / Housing Department
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are scheduled within ten calendar days and on a weekend; allow enough time between the inspection and the move-in date.
requirements: Interior and exterior inspection by Township Code Enforcement
New or currently tagged 2A10BC fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen (checklist still lists it)
GFCI outlets at sinks, washing machines and bathrooms
No open wiring; no holes in walls, ceilings or floors; no cracked or broken windows
Screens in all windows; handrails on interior and exterior stairs; working interior doors
Heating and venting inspection current within 1 year
Application lists the number of bedrooms and the names of everyone who will occupy the unit

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy on sale, one or two family dwelling, per dwelling unit
fees.quote: One or two-family dwellings: One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) a dwelling unit.

fees.label: Reinspection after the second failed reinspection, residential
fees.quote: Upon second reinspection and failure, the fee shall be Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) for residential

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Application for Resale MCCO Certificate (circle Resale), list the bedrooms and everyone who will live there, request an inspection date, and pay $100.00 by cash or check payable to Township of Shrewsbury at the Municipal Office, 1979 Crawford Street (open Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
resale_co.contact_title: Code Enforcement/Housing Department (also listed as Fire Marshal)

evidence.quote: Inspection Fee Schedule for a Certificate of Occupancy upon the Sale, Transfer, Mortgage, Lease or otherwise disposed of shall be as follows:
The certificate is good for 60 days from the time of an approved inspection.
Scheduling will be within ten calendar days and on a weekend.
HEATING A& VENTING INSPECTION (current within 1 year)

resale_co.notes: The Township's certificate of occupancy ordinance dates from April 9, 1985 (amended 1996, 2014 and 2015); fees were updated by Ordinance 2023-03, whose posted copy shows first reading February 14, 2022 and a blank adoption date. The application form (revised 04/2024) covers resale, rental and new-tenant MCCOs and lists the Township's three main complexes (Shrewsbury Arms, Shrewsbury Woods, Alfred Vail Co-op); the Township is about 0.1 square miles, so 1 and 2 family sales are rare. Condo or co-op units sold individually are $100.00 a unit. The Township website spells the officer's name David Boehing (email DBoehing@townshipofshrewsbury.com); the state fire directory spells it Boehnig, and Tinton Falls lists a fire inspector David Boehning. Rent control and the 2023 lead-paint rental ordinance are rental programs, not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke detectors, CO detector and a new or currently tagged 2A10BC kitchen fire extinguisher are checked on the Township's certificate of occupancy checklist (form still lists the extinguisher)

authorities.name: Shrewsbury Township Fire Marshal / Code Enforcement (Shrewsbury Twp Code Enf)
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application or fee is posted. The Township's resale MCCO checklist includes smoke detectors, the CO detector and the fire extinguisher; call the Municipal Office (732-542-0572) to confirm whether a separate smoke/CO certificate is issued and what it costs.

LEAID: 1346-001 Shrewsbury Twp SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Shrewsbury Twp Code Enf Enf Auth. Municipal Fire Official David Boehnig Phone (732) 542-0572

fire_cert.notes: The state fire directory lists Shrewsbury Township Code Enforcement as the smoke detector compliance office with fire official David Boehnig at (732) 542-0572 (a second line shows (732) 741-4200, which is the Shrewsbury Borough number). The Township ordinance page lists Ordinance #2026-05, Providing for Local Enforcement of the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, as Tabled, so the local fire code arrangement may change; check with the Township. P.L.2025, c.19 dropped the extinguisher from the state sale certificate in February 2025, but the Township checklist still lists it.

other_items.label: Heating and venting inspection
other_items.detail: A heating and venting inspection current within one year is on the Township's certificate of occupancy checklist.
